notes: On doors, in shops and stations. Also the word for 'east' and for an airport gate.

examples.tl: Sejdeme se u východu z metra.
examples.en: Let's meet at the metro exit.

notes: One syllable away from východ (exit): v- = in, vý- = out. 'Vstup' is also used for entry.

examples.en: The entrance is on the other side.

notes: On doors: TAM = push (literally 'there', away from you). SEM = pull.

examples.en: The door says PUSH.

notes: On doors: SEM = pull (literally 'to here', toward you). Also: Pojďte sem = come here.

examples.en: SEM means pull, TAM means push.

notes: On shop doors, often with hours: Otevřeno 9–18. 'Nonstop' = open 24 hours.

examples.tl: Otevřeno denně od devíti do šesti.
examples.en: Open daily from nine to six.

notes: On doors. 'Z technických důvodů zavřeno' = closed for technical reasons.

examples.en: Closed on Mondays.

notes: Smoking is banned inside pubs and restaurants and at stops. Zákaz = ban: zákaz vstupu, zákaz focení.

examples.en: Smoking is banned in the restaurant.

notes: Plural on signs (one = toaleta); also 'WC', said 'vé-cé'. Often paid: 10–20 Kč at stations and in malls.

examples.en: The toilets are on the ground floor.

notes: On toilet doors (plural of muž = man). Often just M. Careful: Ž is the women's.

examples.en: Toilets: men on the left, women on the right.

notes: On toilet doors (plural of žena = woman). Often just Ž.

examples.tl: Dveře s písmenem Ž jsou pro ženy.
examples.en: The door with the letter Ž is for women.

notes: The other men's toilet sign (plural of pán). Older places use this pair: Páni / Dámy.

examples.en: The door says Gentlemen.

notes: The other women's toilet sign (plural of dáma).

examples.tl: Toalety pro dámy jsou v prvním patře.
examples.en: The ladies' toilets are on the first floor.

notes: On boards as 'Nást.' At the platform = na nástupišti; from platform 3 = z třetího nástupiště. The track is 'kolej'.

examples.tl: Vlak do Brna odjíždí z třetího nástupiště.
examples.en: The train to Brno leaves from platform three.

notes: On warning signs: Pozor, schod (step); Pozor, zlý pes (fierce dog). Shouted: Pozor! = look out!

examples.en: Mind the step!

notes: Wherever you pay: station ticket windows, a castle box office, a supermarket checkout.

examples.tl: Vstupenky koupíte v pokladně u vchodu.
examples.en: You can buy tickets at the ticket office by the entrance.

notes: In the metro 'Výstup' marks the way up to the street, with street names. Also means getting off a vehicle.

examples.tl: Výstup do ulice Na Příkopě je vpravo.
examples.en: The way out to Na Příkopě street is on the right.

notes: Metro signs: 'Přestup na linku C' = change to line C. In timetables: s přestupem = with a change.

examples.tl: Přestup na linku B je na Můstku.
examples.en: The transfer to line B is at Můstek.

notes: Green signs; also 'únikový východ' (escape exit).

examples.tl: Nouzový východ je na konci chodby.
examples.en: The emergency exit is at the end of the hallway.

notes: Also 'Zákaz vstupu' or 'Nepovolaným vstup zakázán' (no unauthorized entry).

examples.tl: Tady je vstup zakázán, musíme jít jinudy.
examples.en: There's no entry here, we have to go another way.

notes: On lifts, escalators, ATMs and ticket machines.

examples.en: The elevator is out of order.

notes: On ticket sites and concert posters, and on RegioJet connections in summer.

examples.en: Today's tour is sold out.

notes: On toilet locks, car-park boards and guesthouse doors. A waiter says it when every table is taken.

examples.en: Unfortunately everything is taken.

notes: Opposite of obsazeno: on toilet locks and car parks. 'Volné pokoje' = rooms available.

examples.en: There's still room by the window.

notes: On pub doors and stalls: 'Platba pouze v hotovosti' or 'Karty nebereme' (we don't take cards).

examples.en: Payment in cash only.

notes: Short for koruna česká, written after the number: 250 Kč or 250,-. The comma is the decimal mark: 49,90 Kč.

examples.en: Admission 250 crowns, children 150 crowns.

notes: Plural-only: the sign over small food shops. A 'večerka' is a corner shop open late.

examples.tl: Potraviny na rohu mají otevřeno do deseti.
examples.en: The grocery store on the corner is open until ten.

notes: On price tags and in windows: Akce! = on offer. Also means an event. Výprodej = clearance sale.

examples.en: Beer is on offer today.

notes: On fountains and taps. 'Voda není pitná' or 'Nepitná voda' = do not drink.

examples.en: Is this drinking water?

notes: At main stations, staffed or as lockers (úložné skříňky). Handy between check-out and a late train.

examples.tl: Úschovna zavazadel je v přízemí nádraží.
examples.en: The left luggage office is on the ground floor of the station.

notes: On tram and bus stop signs and timetables: the vehicle stops only if you press the button or wave.

examples.tl: Tahle zastávka je na znamení, zmáčkněte tlačítko.
examples.en: This is a request stop, press the button.

notes: Opening-hours shorthand: Po, Út, St, Čt, Pá, So, Ne = Monday to Sunday. 'Denně' = daily.

examples.en: Open Mon–Fri 8–18, Sat 9–12.
